# Catalog submissions (copy-paste kit)

<!-- Generated by scripts/agent-surfaces.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Text and steps for the catalogs that need a person: an account, a web form or
an attestation. [listings.md](listings.md) says which file backs each listing
and tracks status; update its Status column after each submission. Submit only
after a release, so the `plugins` branch carries the current packages.

Shared facts:

- **Name:** Tracetoon
- **One line:** Creates your PR with a description written from the session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush, and an optional one-off comic.
- **Description:** Creates your PR with a description written from the session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush, and an optional one-off comic. Every claim is checked against what your agent actually did, and you approve the PR before it is posted. On 61 real pull requests from 12 repositories, AI judges preferred the descriptions from Tracetoon's evidence graph to its earlier multi-agent workflow 83 to 34 on Codex and 69 to 17 on Claude Code, at 46% and 31% lower cost per PR.
- **Why use it:**
  - **Written from what happened.** Your agent already logged what you asked for, what it changed and which commands ran; Tracetoon writes the description from that record, so it can say why the change was made and what was tested, not just what the diff shows.
  - **Every claim checked.** Each factual sentence has to trace back to the session evidence, independent reviewers check the draft, and the Validation section comes from recorded test and build runs instead of being typed by the model.
  - **Cheaper to write.** A compact, cited evidence brief built in an embedded graph database lets the agent draft without rereading raw logs.
  - **Safe to post.** Private paths and secrets are redacted from the evidence, a leak scan runs before anything is posted, and you approve the PR first.
  - **Follows the house rules.** It reads the repository's PR template, contribution guide and AI-disclosure policy and writes to them.
  - **Works with your agents.** Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush, as an agent skill, a CLI or an MCP server.
  - **A comic on top.** An optional one-off comic about the change, which reviewers actually read.
- **Results:** On 61 real pull requests from 12 repositories, AI judges preferred the descriptions from Tracetoon's evidence graph to its earlier multi-agent workflow 83 to 34 on Codex and 69 to 17 on Claude Code, at 46% and 31% lower cost per PR. (https://tracetoon.ai/evidence-graph-61.html)
- **Repository:** https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon (plugin packages on the `plugins` branch: https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon/tree/plugins)
- **Website:** https://tracetoon.ai
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0
- **Icon:** `assets/tracetoon.png` in each package (square app tile); more sizes in [docs/brand](../brand/README.md)
- **Requirements:** Node.js 18 or later (npx), git, and the GitHub CLI (`gh`) signed in; macOS, Linux or Windows

## Which package goes where

Catalogs that review plugins get a text-only package from the `plugins` branch:
Markdown, JSON, a PNG icon and the licence, running the npm runtime at the
release's exact version (`npx -y tracetoon@1.0.0-rc.38`). The release workflow
publishes that branch, and tags it `plugins/v<version>`, once npm serves the
version. Each package's README.md and REVIEW.md say what runs, what it reads,
writes and sends, and how to check it.

| Catalog | Package (on `plugins`) | What the catalog allows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic plugin directory | `claude/` | Skill, hooks, MCP; a pinned `npx` is held for a reviewer |
| Cursor Marketplace | `cursor/` | Skill, hooks, MCP; every update is reviewed |
| Codex (repo marketplace) | `codex/` | Skill, hooks (after the user trusts them), MCP |
| OpenAI plugin directory | `codex-directory/` (ZIP on each release) | Skill only: no lifecycle hooks, no local MCP |
| Copilot CLI (awesome-copilot) | `agent/` | Skill, hooks, MCP |
| Kiro Powers | `agent/` | Skill and MCP |

## Anthropic plugin directory

1. Sign in at https://claude.ai/directory/manage.
2. Repository `Tracetoon/tracetoon`, branch or tag `plugins`, plugin path `claude`.
3. Category: productivity. Description: the one line above.
4. Expect a reviewer hold on the pinned `npx` hooks and MCP server: the directory
   holds any launcher whose dependencies resolve at install time. REVIEW.md
   answers what the reviewer checks.
5. A directory listing installs as `tracetoon@synced`, which Claude Code's
   `<claude-code-hint />` doesn't recommend; leave `CLAUDE_CODE_HINT_ENABLED` off
   unless Tracetoon joins an official marketplace.

## Cursor Marketplace

1. Open https://cursor.com/marketplace/publish and submit https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon.
2. In the notes: the plugin is the `cursor` folder on the `plugins` branch
   (`main` holds source); it ships no binaries and runs `npx -y tracetoon@<version>`.
3. Description: the one line above. Logo: `cursor/assets/tracetoon.png`.

## OpenAI Codex plugin directory

The repo marketplace works without review: `codex plugin marketplace add Tracetoon/tracetoon`
(package `codex/`, with hooks). The public directory accepts no lifecycle hooks,
and local MCP servers only from approved partners, so it gets the skill alone;
needs the OpenAI org owner, identity verification and a video:

1. Download `tracetoon-codex-directory.zip` from the latest release.
2. Upload it at https://platform.openai.com/plugins and choose **Skills only**.
3. Display name: Tracetoon. Short description (30 characters):
   PRs written from agent logs. Category: Developer Tools.
4. Long description:

   > Creates your PR with a description written from the session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush, and an optional one-off comic. Every claim is checked against what your agent actually did, and you approve the PR before it is posted. On 61 real pull requests from 12 repositories, AI judges preferred the descriptions from Tracetoon's evidence graph to its earlier multi-agent workflow 83 to 34 on Codex and 69 to 17 on Claude Code, at 46% and 31% lower cost per PR. It creates or updates the PR with the GitHub CLI; needs git and gh signed in. Comic images go to an image service only after you approve one.

5. Test cases. Should start Tracetoon:
   1. "Open a PR for this branch."
   2. "Create a pull request that describes what I changed and how it was tested."
   3. "Run gh pr create for this branch."
   4. "Write the pull request description for this branch from my session."
   5. "Update the description of PR 12 with Tracetoon."

   Should not start it:
   1. "Fix the failing test in src/parser.ts."
   2. "What does Tracetoon do?"
   3. "Review this pull request for bugs."
6. Video walkthrough (about 2 minutes): ask Codex to open a PR on a small branch;
   show the brief, the reviewed description and the created PR with its comic;
   end on `tracetoon off` to show it can be turned off.

## GitHub Copilot (awesome-copilot)

Submit through the issue form at https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot (not a
PR to `plugins/external.json`), naming a release tag and its full commit SHA:

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon, path `agent`
- **Ref:** `plugins/v<version>` and the 40-character SHA it points at
  (`git rev-parse plugins/v<version>^{commit}`)
- Checks it runs: the Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest, `vally lint` and a Copilot CLI
  install smoke test.

## Kiro Powers

Submit at https://kiro.dev/registry/submit/?type=power once a final (non-rc)
version is out: the form asks for generally available MCP servers. Repository
https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon, folder `agent` on the `plugins` branch; the 3–4 word use case:
"PR descriptions from logs". Users can already add it with Powers → **Add
Custom Power** → **Import power from GitHub**.

## awesome-claude-code

The list accepts recommendations **only from people, through the web issue form**
(not the `gh` CLI, not an agent), and its maintainer favours projects that
already have users. Submit it yourself, last, and tick the checklist only for
what you actually did:
https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code/issues/new?template=recommend-resource.yml

- **Display Name:** Tracetoon
- **Category:** Open Source Contribution & Maintenance
- **Link:** https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon
- **Author Name:** Tracetoon
- **Author Link:** https://github.com/Tracetoon
- **Description:** Writes GitHub pull request descriptions from Claude Code session logs, checks each claim against what ran, and can add a one-off comic.

## No form needed

- **skills.sh:** ranks by installs through the `skills` CLI: `npx skills add Tracetoon/tracetoon#release --skill tracetoon -g -y`.
- **MCP Registry:** the release workflow publishes `server.json` once the npm package
  exists and the repository variable `MCP_REGISTRY_PUBLISH` is set.
- **GitHub Copilot agent finder:** a PR to `github/agentfinder-catalog` adding
  `catalog/tracetoon/tracetoon.json` (from `catalog/agentfinder/`) and the icon.
- **Gemini CLI gallery:** the `gemini-cli-extension` repository topic; the gallery
  crawls tagged repositories daily.
- **awesome-agent-skills:** wait for community usage, then a PR titled
  `Add skill: Tracetoon/tracetoon`.
